records.observation_summary: The firm failed to establish a stability testing program for drug products, lacked finished product testing for strength and quality, failed to establish a quality control unit with written procedures for production, testing, and maintenance, failed to calibrate equipment used for weighing ingredients, and failed to maintain complete batch production and control records with quality control review.

observations.full_details: Specifically, your firm has failed to calibrate your (b)(4) calibration weight and the (b)(4) (b)(4) balances used to weigh active pharmaceutical ingredients and components for your drug products. Additionally, there are no written procedures describing the requirements for the calibration of the balances and calibration weight.

records.observation_summary: The IRB failed to follow written procedures for the initial review of research, specifically regarding the distribution of materials and the documentation of responses to member concerns. The IRB also failed to ensure informed consent documents adequately described experimental procedures. Furthermore, the IRB failed to conduct reviews at fully convened meetings with a majority present, instead relying on subcommittee approvals and block votes without documented discussion. Finally, the IRB failed to maintain adequate documentation of its activities, including discrepancies between written minutes and audio recordings regarding member conflicts of interest and abstentions.

observations.full_details: During the 9/18/00 meeting, an IRB member had a conflict of interest on two studies; while minutes recorded abstention, the audiotape did not. During the 1/18/00 meeting, minutes recorded 11 members present with three having conflicts on six studies, but the audio recording did not capture the discussion or the abstentions. During the 3/19/01 meeting, minutes recorded 12 members present with three having conflicts on ten studies; while minutes indicated one member abstained, the audio recording did not reflect that any of the three members abstained.

records.observation_summary: The inspection identified multiple deficiencies in the firm's aseptic processing operations, including inadequate environmental monitoring, lack of sterile filter integrity testing, insufficient media fill simulations, poor gowning and aseptic practices, inadequate cleaning and sanitization, and a lack of scientific validation for sterility, potency, and stability testing programs.

observations.full_details: The cleaning and sanitization activities performed in the aseptic processing areas are not adequate.

records.observation_summary: The inspection revealed significant deficiencies in the firm's quality, laboratory, production, and facilities systems. Key issues included failure to timely file Field Alert Reports, inadequate investigations into product complaints and quality failures, lack of comprehensive training and qualification for personnel, deficient laboratory test methods and controls, inadequate environmental monitoring and sterility assurance practices, improper equipment maintenance and calibration, and poor facility maintenance including pest control issues.

observations.full_details: Representative samples are not taken of each shipment of each lot of components for testing or examination. Specifically, a) Endotoxin testing of PVC film (e.g., R-24 Double Wound 96-2439) following extrusion prior to the slitting and bag fabricator is conducted on a (b) (4) basis and per 94.B-024 uses a minimum of (b) (4) of PVC film from each Extruder (i.e., #s 1 & 2). Test procedure 94.B-024 does not identify where samples are collected from on the master roll per lot within the 24-hour period before the slitting/bag fabrication and reads to collect a PVC film sample representative of the lot (per 24 hours). Your firm collected a sample consisting of two feet from the master roll, which was said to be sampled from the end of the run lot. There is no indication if this is a statistically valid sample representative of the lot over a 24 hour period (e.g. beginning, middle and end of the extrusion process). b) Each shipment received for commodities (with the same lot number) are not routinely sampled for testing with the receipt of each shipment when received on different dates. For examples, see 10a - c above. In addition, there is no raw data to support placement of commodities on a reduced testing program whereby one lot of commodity per commodity is tested annually for Incoming Quality (e.g., visual, physical, dimensions, and particulates). c) Testing is not completed on a representative sample that is statistically valid for APIs. For examples: i. Dextrose USP Monohydrate: Lot #16011 JR, received on 04/05/12, included (b) (4) containers and one container was tested for ID; Lot 16010JR, received on 04/05/12 included (b) (4) containers and one container was tested for ID; and Lot 09042 JR01, received on 09/23/11 included (b) (4) containers and one container was tested for full monograph testing. The remaining(b) (4 containers were composited (i.e., containers 2-10, 11-20, 21-30, 31-40, 41-50, 51-60, 61-70, 71-80, 81-90, 91-100, and 101-108) and were tested for specific rotation, color and appearance. Dextrose USP Monohydrate API was put on skip attribute/reduced testing in 1995 and said to be tested at your Rocky Mount facility; however, the data used in the qualification for skip attribute/reduced testing could not be located. No other raw data was provided. ii. Sodium Chloride, USP: Lot #15024 JR, received on 03/19/12, included (b) (4) containers and one container was tested for full monograph testing. iii. Sodium Chloride, USP: Lot 17056 JR, received on 05/24/12, included (b) (4) containers and one container was tested for full monograph testing. (containers from the (b) (4) containers were reassigned lot 17057 JR. Lot 17057 JR included testing container 7 and a composite from containers 1-6 for color and appearance. Container 7 was used for full monograph testing excluding ID since this was tested on lot 17056 JR. d) Lack of documentation on all lots of 70% IPA prepared from 99% IPA with purified water per BCLN0004 for "Disinfectants Dilutions and Labeling Procedures". In addition, there is no incoming analytical testing of IPA 99% conducted and no analytical testing conducted on prepared 70% IPA (except bioburden). Your firm does not track all lots of 70% IPA prepared (e.g., labels are kept for prepared 70% IPA used in clean room ISO 7 areas for use on operator gloves and/or when used to clean areas in ISO 7 and ISO 8 areas for product contact surfaces (e.g., filling nozzles)). In addition, there is no validation of the C of A received with IPA 99% and no identification exam listed on the C of A.

records.observation_summary: The inspection identified significant deficiencies in aseptic processing procedures, including inadequate equipment sanitization, improper operator behavior in clean rooms, and insufficient environmental monitoring controls. Additionally, the firm failed to implement effective corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs) for recurring environmental monitoring excursions, with investigations lacking adequate root cause analysis and follow-up.

observations.full_details: Operators do not perform inspection of the RABS (b)(4) after installation as required by SOP BF/FM/SOP/182 and SOP BF/FM/SOP/180. An operator in the Grade C area failed to sanitize the RABS (b)(4) after an open (b)(4) operation, contrary to SOP BF/FM/SOP/180 and SOP BF/FM/SOP/194. SOP BF/FM/SOP/180 is inadequate as it lacks instructions to prevent contamination during equipment transfer; an employee was observed squatting to retrieve a vessel from a lower shelf and placing it into the open RABS. Environmental monitoring is not performed at the location where dosing vessels are placed into the RABS. SOP BF/QA/SOP/002 lacks temperature criteria or secure storage locations for media fill units during the time gap between sealing and incubation. The visual inspection SOP is inadequate regarding rejected vial tracking; rejected vials were found in a drawer without proper documentation on the bench sheet. Sterile forceps are stored in a manner that limits sterile access, and operators place sterile (b)(4) face down on work surfaces in Grade B areas.

records.observation_summary: The firm failed to adhere to Salmonella Enteritidis (SE) prevention requirements, including inadequate cleaning and disinfection of poultry houses, failure to conduct required environmental testing, and use of unapproved testing methods. Additionally, the firm lacked comprehensive SE prevention plans, failed to implement existing fly and rodent monitoring procedures, did not maintain required refrigeration records, and failed to ensure equipment cross-contamination controls and proper record identification.

observations.full_details: Your firm's document entitled, "Procedure: Environmental Sampling for SE" (created 6/24/2010 and revised 05/27/2011) states "(b) (4)". It also (b) (4). (b) (4). Management provided an internet print out listing currently used sampling tools for environmental sampling. The document and management indicated they use (b) (4) for all environmental testing. Using (b) (4) (b) (4) as a tool for environmental sampling for Salmonella Enteritidis is not recognized by the FDA as an equivalent method.

records.observation_summary: The inspection revealed significant deficiencies in equipment cleaning and maintenance, aseptic processing procedures, environmental monitoring, air filtration systems, data integrity and backup, investigation of discrepancies, and process controls. Specific issues included visible residues on cleaned equipment, improper aseptic techniques by personnel, inadequate validation of aseptic processes, lack of airflow visualization and pressure monitoring, deficient environmental monitoring programs, missing engineering diagrams for air handling, failure to maintain data backups, inadequate investigations into sterilization failures and consumer complaints, and lack of scientific rationale for process parameters.

observations.full_details: CCTV systems are not used to record production operations. The firm has not performed vendor audits for the German contractor providing garment qualification or the supplier of biological indicators. The Quality Unit has not reviewed or approved the 2008 I/OQ documents for the Building Management System.

records.observation_summary: The inspection revealed significant deficiencies in aseptic processing and sterilization validation, including inadequate media fills, smoke studies, and sterilization validation for equipment and glassware. There were failures to investigate unexplained discrepancies, such as HEPA filter leaks, microbial contamination, and product defects. Additionally, the firm lacked proper cleaning and maintenance procedures, failed to validate laboratory testing methods, lacked adequate production and process controls, and failed to maintain environmental monitoring documentation.

observations.full_details: Your firm is unable to provide documentation of positive pressure monitoring in the clean room during sterile drug production for the time period prior to March 2018.

records.observation_summary: The inspection revealed significant deficiencies in the firm's aseptic processing operations, including inadequate gowning, lack of environmental monitoring, and failure to validate sterilization processes. The firm also failed to conduct thorough investigations into batch failures, lacked written quality control procedures, and did not perform required stability testing. Additionally, drug product labels were found to be missing mandatory information required for outsourcing facilities.

observations.full_details: Specifically, your firm has no scientific data to justify the assigned Beyond Use Date for the following sterile products: 90 day Beyond Use Date for Testosterone Cypionate Injectable; 30 day Beyond Use Date for Gentamicin Irrigation Solution.

records.observation_summary: The inspection revealed significant deficiencies in the firm's quality control unit, specifically regarding the investigation of out-of-specification (OOS) results, particularly for foreign matter in sterile products. The firm failed to perform thorough root cause analyses, implement effective corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), and maintain adequate documentation for batch failures and deviations. Additionally, there were failures in process validation, equipment maintenance and calibration, environmental monitoring, and the management of incoming components. The firm also lacked standardized procedures for critical operations such as media fills, re-labeling, and adverse event reporting, and failed to ensure that annual product reviews were accurate and comprehensive.

observations.full_details: Written procedures (AA204, QA101) do not adequately describe instructions for aborting or invalidating batches. There is no procedure for the storage of integral rejects before transfer, and no requirement for QA to approve pen amendments to batch records, leading to unauthorized changes by production personnel.

records.observation_summary: The inspection revealed systemic failures in analytical method validation, process validation, data integrity, and quality control oversight. The firm failed to validate numerous test methods for drug products and APIs, lacked scientific rationale for cleaning and hold-time procedures, and failed to maintain adequate documentation for investigations, deviations, and annual product reviews. Furthermore, computer systems lacked necessary controls to prevent data manipulation, and raw material testing was insufficient to ensure compliance with specifications.

observations.full_details: Drug products are not stored under appropriate conditions of humidity. Hygroscopic products like Pyridostigmine and Colestipol are stored in warehouses without established control limits or monitoring procedures to prevent moisture-induced degradation.

records.establishment_type: National Headquarters of a Licensed Blood Bank
records.observation_summary: The inspection revealed systemic failures in the investigation of employee allegations regarding recordkeeping irregularities, inadequate oversight of donor deferral processes, failure to maintain accurate inventory and distribution systems for blood products, and ineffective corrective actions for known quality and safety issues. The firm failed to ensure that unsuitable blood products were quarantined and not reissued, and did not maintain adequate software controls or validation for its National Biomedical Computer System (NBCS). Additionally, the firm's hotline and internal audit processes were found to be insufficient in identifying, investigating, and resolving significant quality and safety concerns.

observations.full_details: Only a one-page memo was provided, which lacked documentation of the assessment.
Inspections in 2001 found the problem of releasing donors from hold before making changes was continuing. The BSL stated 'No training is required'.

records.observation_summary: The firm failed to adequately investigate sterility failures and product complaints, often attributing them to customer handling without scientific evidence. Aseptic processing areas showed significant facility maintenance issues, including water incursions and damaged surfaces. Smoke studies and media fills were inadequate to validate aseptic processes. Cleaning and disinfection procedures were deficient, and equipment maintenance and record-keeping practices were insufficient. Additionally, data integrity gaps were identified in computer systems, and annual product reviews were not conducted in a timely manner.

observations.full_details: Annual product reviews remain in draft status months after the review period ended. A significant portion of 2025 annual product reviews for US products were late or incomplete.

records.observation_summary: The inspection revealed significant deficiencies in sterile drug production, including poor aseptic techniques by personnel, inadequate environmental monitoring and control, lack of sterility testing and growth promotion testing, improper facility design and maintenance, failure to investigate sterility failures and complaints, and inadequate documentation of production and stability testing.

observations.full_details: Your firm has used non-sterile wipes to clean and disinfect ISO 5 hoods and the ISO 7 clean room throughout 2013. Additionally, your firm has not rotated cleaning solutions to account for sporicidal agents.

records.observation_summary: The firm failed to conduct thorough investigations into sterility failures, specifically regarding Gram Positive Rods (Bacillus species), by failing to evaluate potential root causes in the production facility, neglecting to include comprehensive environmental monitoring data, and failing to implement robust corrective and preventive actions to mitigate contamination risks in aseptic compounding areas.

observations.full_details: Specifically, your investigations into sterility failures were not conducted thoroughly to evaluate potential root causes in the production facility and to implement robust corrective and preventative action plans to mitigate sterility risks to products. During Oct 2021 to Dec 2021, two sterility failures were observed on the finished product sterility testing, identified to be Gram Positive Rods (Bacillus licheniformis and Niallia circulans), belonging to Bacillus species of family. Sterility failures were investigated under #OOS-OOT-2021-0044 on 20Oct2021 for 8mg Norepinephrine in 0.9% Sodium Chloride (250mL IV Bag), Lot# (b)(4); and #OOS-OOT-2021-0054 on 02Dec2021 for 1 Unit/mL Vasopressin 0.9% Sodium Chloride (50mL), Lot (b)(4). Investigations into sterility failures did not include comprehensive evaluations of environmental monitoring results from the compounding area and personnel; and the review of the environmental excursions were not extended to all excursions from all sources during this time period. Your failure to identify elevated environmental excursions in the aseptic compounding areas (with spore forming microorganisms) as a potential contamination source, insufficient corrective actions were implemented to mitigate spore forming microorganisms in the environment and to protect product sterility during aseptic operations. During our review of the environmental trend report for (b)(4), we observed increased environmental excursion levels from compounding personnel gloves/gowns during October 2021 with at least 13 out of 18 microorganisms identified to be Gram Positive Rods, belonging to Bacillus species family.

records.observation_summary: The inspection identified failures to maintain site-specific Salmonella Enteritidis (SE) prevention plans for multiple egg-producing facilities and a failure to include required documentation regarding the procurement of chicks from SE-monitored breeder flocks within the SE prevention plan.

observations.full_details: Failure to maintain a Salmonella Enteritidis prevention plan (SE) specific for each egg producing site. Specifically, the layer facilities indicated below lack the required site specific SE plans: 11995 Croton Road Croton, Ohio 43013 and 11492 Westley Chapel Road Croton, Ohio 43013.

records.observation_summary: The firm exhibits significant deficiencies in aseptic processing, including inadequate cleaning and disinfection procedures, lack of environmental monitoring, and improper personnel gowning. Furthermore, the firm fails to perform required sterility and pyrogen testing for batches, lacks written investigations for unexplained discrepancies and test failures, fails to maintain complete batch production records, and operates in an environment lacking appropriate HEPA filtration.

observations.full_details: The ISO 8 room in-which the ISO 5 (b)(4) is located, does not have HEPA filter units at the air supply vents for the area. The filter located in the return air grate is not sufficient to ensure adequate filtration of the air circulating through the area.

records.observation_summary: The inspection identified significant deficiencies in the firm's quality systems, including inadequate investigations into unexplained discrepancies, lack of method validation for release testing, deficient environmental monitoring in aseptic processing areas, incomplete laboratory records, failure to retain required reserve samples, and non-compliance with outsourcing facility registration and bulk drug substance sourcing requirements.

observations.full_details: Your outsourcing facility did not submit a report to FDA upon initial registration as an outsourcing facility identifying the drugs compounded during the previous six month period. Specifically, the following products were compounded and not identified on your reports dated December 31, 2020 and/or June 30, 2021. Examples include, but are not limited to: Vitamin D (b)(4)/ml injection, Buprenorphine 0.4 mg/ml injectable, Alpha lipoic acid 25 mg/ml injection, Sildenafil 110 mg capsules, Tadalifil 10 mg troches, Dihydroepiandosterone 58 mg and pregnenolone 250 mg capsules, Dihydroepiandosterone 12.5 mg and pregnenolone 100 mg capsules, Dihydroepiandosterone 25 mg and pregnenolone 100 mg capsules, Minoxidil 5%, tretinoin 0.01%, triamcinolone 0.1% topical solution, Minoxidil 5%, tretinoin 0.01%, finasteride 2.5% topical solution, Naltrexone 2 mg capsules, Dimercapto Succinate acid 250 mg capsules, Liothyronine 35 mcg capsules, Liothyronine 10 mcg capsules, Benzocaine 20%, lidocaine 8%, and tetracaine 8% topical gel, Benzocaine 20%, lidocaine 8%, and tetracaine 4% topical gel, Lidocaine 23% and tetracaine 7% topical gel, Lidocaine 4%, epinephrine 0.05%, tetracaine 0.5% gel, Lidocaine 1% preservative-free buffered with 8.4% sodium bicarbonate injectable, Alprostadil 10 mcg/ml penile injectable, Tri-Mix Alprostadil 20 mcg, papaverine 30 mg, and phentolamine 4 mg/ml, Tri-Mix Alprostadil 30 meg, papaverine 30 mg, and phentolamine 2 mg/ml, Phosphatidyl choline 5% and deoxycholate 4.2% injectable, Testosterone 0.15% topical cream, Testosterone 8 mg/ml topical gel, Prednisolone 1% ophthalmic drops, Mebendazole 100 mg capsules, CoQ10 20 mg/ml in oil injectable, Liposupreme: (b)(4) mg/ml injectable, Myer's cocktail: preservative-free vitamin C (b)(4); magnesium (b)(4) calcium (b)(4) (b)(4) injectable, 7-Keto DHEA injectable, Acetyl cysteine 200 mg/ml injectable, Estriol 2 mg suppositories, Estriol 2 mg and testosterone 10 mg per gram topical gel, Semorelin acetate 1 mg/ml injection, Amphotericin B 50 mg, chloramphenicol 500 mg, hydrocortisone 10 mg/g otic powder, Acetyl D-glucosamine 100 mg/ml injectable, Hydroxocobalamin 1,000 mcg/ml injection.

records.observation_summary: The firm failed to maintain adequate procedures for aseptic processing, including media fills, environmental monitoring, and cleaning. The quality unit failed to conduct investigations for non-sterile results and patient complaints, and lacked proper oversight of stability testing, batch records, and labeling requirements. Additionally, the firm failed to report all compounded products as required for an outsourcing facility.

observations.full_details: Results of stability testing are not used in determining expiration dates. Specifically, your outsourcing facility lacked valid analytical and sterility data to support the 90-day beyond use date (BUD) assigned to repackaged syringes of preservative-free Avastin. The BUD was based on scientific journals not specific to the firm's operations.

records.observation_summary: The firm failed to maintain adequate quality control, sterility assurance, and environmental monitoring systems. Significant issues included the release of drug product lots that failed batch yield and particulate matter specifications, inadequate investigation of microbiological contamination and customer complaints, poor aseptic technique by operators, and deficient documentation practices. Additionally, the firm lacked robust electronic data integrity controls, failed to perform necessary method transfers and stability studies, and maintained facilities in a state of disrepair.

observations.full_details: Batch production and control records do not include complete information relating to the production and control of each batch. A. Your Quality Unit failed to have procedures in place to maintain production and control records. You use laminated plastic sheets (Pallet IDs) to record batch production information, which are not maintained. B. Large quantities of paper documents from production and testing in the record storage room were not reviewed, scanned, or saved into the appropriate batch records.

records.observation_summary: The inspection revealed significant deficiencies in the firm's sterile drug production processes, including inadequate validation of sterilization cycles, improper gowning and aseptic technique, deficient environmental monitoring and cleaning systems, lack of proper facility design and air pressure control, inadequate instrument calibration, and insufficient laboratory testing for sterility, potency, stability, and raw material quality.

observations.full_details: a) Media fills performed for injectable drug products do not simulate the entire production process including but not limited to: all process steps and manipulations, aseptic filling without terminal filtration, and all container/closure systems used for drug products. Additionally, media fills do not include a challenge of worst case conditions including but not limited to: duration of aseptic processing and representative batch size. b) Integrity testing specifications set by your firm for the Supor 25 and 32 mm syringe filters (0.22 um) have not been verified by the manufacturer or otherwise validated. These filters are used as sterilizing filters in production of injectable drug products. c) Sterilization cycles using the Tuttnauer Tabletop Autoclave Model 2340 have not been validated for terminally sterilized finished drug products. Temperature mapping, heat penetration, and loading configurations have not been evaluated to ensure sterilization of finished drug products, equipment, and containers/closures. d) Sterilization cycles using the All American Model 75X Electric Pressure Steam Sterilizer (serial number 0001199) have not been validated for terminally sterilized finished drug products. Temperature mapping, heat penetration, and loading configurations have not been evaluated to ensure sterilization of finished drug products, equipment, and container/closures. Additionally, the 75X steam sterilizer has not been qualified and no calibration/verification has been performed for the temperature and pressure instruments. e) Sterilization and depyrogenation cycles using the Yamato DK-43 dry heat oven have not been validated for sterilization and depyrogenation of containers, equipment, and powders used in drug products. Temperature mapping, heat penetration, and loading configurations have not been evaluated to ensure sterilization and depyrogenation of containers, closures, equipment, and drug components. Endotoxin challenges have only been performed for one cycle (glassware cycle), however your firm uses another cycle for powders which has not been challenged. Powders intended to be sterilized in this dry heat oven are then mixed into final injectable drug products without further sterilization. Additionally, the dry heat oven has not been qualified and no calibration/verification has been performed for the temperature and pressure instruments.

records.establishment_type: Drug substance and drug product manufacturer
records.observation_summary: The inspection identified significant deficiencies in aseptic processing, environmental monitoring, visual inspection procedures, data integrity, and quality unit oversight. Key issues include poor aseptic techniques during filling operations and media fills, inadequate mold control and monitoring in classified areas, lack of statistical rigor in visual inspection and AQL testing, deficient electronic data management and audit trail reviews, and failures in the deviation management and CAPA systems.

observations.full_details: A. QA unit does not review electronic data or audit trails, relying only on paper records. B. Empower 3 CDS data management is deficient; methods are stored in multiple folders, and QC review does not reconcile all sequences. C. Analyst permissions allow viewing of quantitation fields before saving data. D. QC testing systems lack access controls; a pH meter was found without user/password protection.

records.observation_summary: The firm caused violative drug residues in cattle sold for slaughter due to improper drug use, administered animal drugs in a manner contrary to label directions without a valid veterinary client-patient relationship, and failed to maintain complete treatment records, specifically regarding the route of administration and dosage for drugs administered to dairy cows.

observations.full_details: Specifically, 1. You do not routinely record the route of administration of each drug administered to the dairy cows on your farm. a. For example, you medicated a dairy cow identified with Ear Tag # (b)(4) with Penicillin (Pen G, PEN) on 11/13/2008. Your computer generated and written record does not indicate the route of administration. b. For example, you medicated a dairy cow identified with Ear Tag # (b)(4) with Sulfadimethoxine (SDM) on 08/05/2009. Your computer generated and written record does not indicate the route of administration. c. For example, you medicated a dairy cow identified with Ear Tag # (b)(4) with Polyflex (Poly) on 08/04/2009 and 08/05/2009. Your computer generated and written record does not indicate the route of administration. 2. You do not always record the dosage of each drug administered to the dairy cows on your farm. a. For example, you medicated a dairy cow identified with Ear Tag # (b)(4) with Flunixin (Banamine; Benamine, BN) on 11/13/2008. Your written and computer generated record does not indicate the dosage of Flunixin (Banamine) that was administered to this dairy cow. b. For example, you medicated a dairy cow identified with Ear Tag # (b)(4) with Polyflex (Poly) on 08/05/2009. Your computer generated and written record does not indicate the dosage of Polyflex that was administered to this dairy cow. c. For example, you medicated a dairy cow identified with Ear Tag # (b)(4) with Penicillin (Pen G, Pen) on 08/08/2009. Your computer generated and written record does not indicate the dosage of Penicillin that was administered to this dairy cow.

Environmental monitoring practices were insufficient, with failures to investigate out-of-specification results and improper sampling procedures. The quality control unit failed to implement robust visual inspection programs or ensure sterility testing was completed prior to product release. Additionally, product labels lacked required adverse event reporting information and directions for use.
